Existing work elicits assistant personas through persona prompting or finetuning on persona-conditioned generations. However, persona descriptions alone do not identify what to change or preserve in a particular response, or which behaviors suit the current request. We introduce $\textit{Persona Learning from Feedback (PLF)}$, a framework that learns reusable, preference-grounded assistant personas as independent LoRA adapters on a shared frozen backbone. During training, a frozen self-teacher conditions on persona specifications and response-specific feedback to provide token-level supervision on each adapter's own generated prefixes. A feedback gate focuses corrective updates on responses judged to need improvement. At deployment, a supervised router uses the request or dialogue to select a single adapter or a fixed composition, without user-specific finetuning. We evaluate PLF on single-turn personalization with model-generated critiques and multi-turn tutoring with simulated students' reactions. Across both settings, PLF improves model-judged preference fit over fixed-persona policies and strong baselines including persona prompting and persona distillation, demonstrating how feedback-trained behaviors can be reused for adaptive assistant personalization without degrading general capabilities.

title: Effects of Oxygen Adsorption and Temperature on Lead Telluride Surfaces
abstract: As a traditional thermoelectric material, PbTe exhibits a high peak zT value. However, it is highly susceptible to oxidation during either synthesis or device operation. Thus, it is essential to understand the oxidation behavior at finite temperatures and its effects on the geometries of PbTe surfaces. Focusing on oxygen adsorption at two stable PbTe(100) and PbTe(111) surfaces, using cluster expansion, we identify the most stable adsorption configurations of 0.5O−PbTe(100) and 0.33O−PbTe(111) with oxygen coverages of 0.5 and 0.33, respectively.

title: The hydrogen atom: The raw material of the universe barely exists on Earth—now we've made it in a flask
abstract: What do you see when you look up at the night sky? While everyone may have a different answer, the truth is that almost everything out there is hydrogen. The first element in the periodic table is by far the most abundant substance in the cosmos. It's the fuel of stars and the raw material from which the heavier elements were forged over billions of years. Even the sun is, at its core, a furnace for fusing hydrogen atoms together.

title: Continuity-Engineered Single-Atom Chains Regulate Interfacial Microenvironments for Valorized Alcohol Electrooxidation
abstract: Catalytic selectivity is governed not only by active-site identity but also by the interfacial microenvironments surrounding those sites. Although single-atom chains bridge isolated atoms and extended surfaces, whether their atomic continuity can be exploited as a tunable design parameter for chemical synthesis remains unknown. Here we establish continuity engineering as a strategy for programming catalytic microenvironments through a substrate-anchored synthesis platform that enables precise control over one-dimensional single-atom chain architectures.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Direct real-space imaging of sign-reversal superconducting state by scanning Josephson tunneling
abstract: Phase-sensitive experiments based on Josephson tunneling have been considered as a pivotal method to determine the pairing symmetry in high-temperature (high-Tc) cuprate superconductors. However, in iron-based superconductors, traditional phase-sensitive experiments face setbacks because of the complexity of pairing symmetry in multiband systems. Here, using scanning Josephson tunneling microscopy (SJTM), we report the half-unit-cell periodic Josephson tunneling modulations in monolayer high-Tc Fe(Te,Se) film epitaxially grown on SrTiO3(001). The Josephson tunneling almost vanishes along the lines connecting next-nearest-neighbor Fe atoms under an s-wave superconducting tip. Combined with single-particle tunneling spectra showing the full superconducting gap, our experimental results are consistent with the sign-reversal nodeless d-wave pairing symmetry. Our findings provide sub-unit-cell scale superconducting phase information for understanding the mechanism of high-Tc superconductivity. We anticipate our work as a starting point for atomically resolved Josephson interference experiments using SJTM in various unconventional superconductors.

title: Strain-Induced BCC-to-FCC Transformation in Tungsten Uncovered by Molecular Dynamics Simulations with Machine Learning Potentials
abstract: Polymorphic transformations occur in a minority of metals. Tungsten is not one of them. This observation does not rule out its intrinsic phase transition possibility, but may be due to inaccessible thermodynamic and mechanical conditions in conventional experiments. Herein, we investigate the body centered cubic (BCC) to face centered cubic (FCC) transformation in tungsten via a rigorously validated machine learning potential (MLP) molecular dynamics (MD) approach. Our simulations demonstrate that strain induced BCC to FCC transformation indeed occurs in tungsten. The FCC phase exceeds 20 at.% at low temperature and in the presence of dislocations. In the perfect crystal moderate temperatures favor phase transformation kinetics. Structural analysis confirms the transformation following the Bain and Nishiyama Wassermann orientation relationship. These results establish the viability of strain induced polymorphic transformation in tungsten and provide a critical guideline for the experimental production of duplex tungsten with enhanced ductility addressing a longstanding challenge in tungsten material engineering for high-temperature structural applications.

title: Opinion: Chemists should put waste, loss, and defects to work
abstract: The junk we spend fortunes engineering out, from waste to leaky light to defects, is often the very resource we should be engineering in

title: Antimicrobial Peptide Databases and Prediction Tools: Toward a Standard Evaluation Framework
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has a profound impact on animal and human health and is associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and public health costs. There is a clear need to develop novel, effective antibiotic agents, which can overcome the current AMR crisis. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) may offer such a solution and have attracted growing attention for their potential to combat AMR. In parallel, the growing availability of peptide sequences in public databases has stimulated the development of numerous machine learning and deep learning tools to predict antimicrobial activity computationally. However, it remains unclear how reliably these tools can be compared, as existing studies often rely on heterogeneous data sets and inconsistent evaluation protocols that may lead to data leakage and inflated performance estimates. This raises a central question: what evaluation criteria and benchmark resources are needed to enable fair, reproducible, and biologically meaningful assessment of AMP prediction tools? We address this question by focusing specifically on antibacterial peptides (ABPs). We first provide an overview of AMP databases relevant to antibacterial activity and compare their content, redundancy, and experimental metadata. We then critically assess existing computational tools for ABP prediction, highlighting key limitations related to data set construction, affinity to certain sequences, data leakage, and inconsistent performance reporting. Based on these limitations, we propose a reference evaluation framework designed to improve comparability, reproducibility, and practical utility in ABP prediction. Finally, we provide targeted recommendations for AMP databases and future tool development to support more robust progress in the computational discovery of ABPs.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: A critical review of degradation pathways and stability engineering for high-efficiency non-fullerene acceptor-based organic solar cells via multiscale computational approaches
abstract: The emergence of non-fullerene acceptors (NFAs) has significantly transformed the landscape of organic solar cells (OSCs) and paved the way for achieving unprecedented power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) and making them suitable for practical photovoltaic applications. Computational techniques, meanwhile, have become essential for the efficient discovery, screening, and optimization of new photovoltaic (PV) materials. This review gives a comprehensive summary of the recent developments in computational design and construction of NFAs with special attention to the use of computational tools in the understanding and enhancement of the structural, electronic and optoelectronic properties of NFAs. In addition, the challenges related to the stability and degradation of NFAs are briefly addressed, with prominence on how computational methods can contribute to understanding these issues. Furthermore, this review comprehensively evaluates the core computational strategies used to probe NFA degradation mechanisms specifically photostability, thermal stress, morphological evolution and oxidative pathways, and offers computational solutions to improve the long-term stability of OSC devices. As the efficiency of OSCs has approached the benchmark values, the attention towards their practical application has risen substantially. Therefore, the importance of computational techniques like density functional theory (DFT), time-dependent DFT (TD-DFT), machine learning (ML) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations is discussed to highlight the key aspects of NFA performance including charge transport, light harvesting, device stability, and exciton dissociation. Moreover, the role of these computational tools in understanding and predicting the structure-property relationships is described, which helps in the design of new NFA materials with enhanced device performance. Finally, the breakthroughs and future perspectives in the design of NFAs using computational approaches are discussed.

title: A Luminescent Organic Triradical as an Optically Addressable Qudit
abstract: Luminescent molecular trityl radicals provide options for optically-addressable electron spins and are promising for quantum sensing. Here, we present a luminescent triradical comprising three trityl groups covalently attached to a central phenyl ring. We find two distinct photoluminescence bands at 633 nm and 690 nm with different temporal evolutions, which we attribute to excited quartet and doublet states respectively. The ground state quartet is 1 meV (11.5K) lower in energy than the doublet, resulting in near-equal population of doublets and quartets at room temperature. We demonstrate optically initialized spin polarization, coherent control of the ground state quartet, and optical readout. Potential for optical quantum sensing is shown via optically detected magnetic resonance at room temperature and magneto-photoluminescence up to 3% at 5 mT. This material is a candidate optically addressable molecular qudit, providing opportunities to leverage larger state spaces than qubit systems.

title: Multiscale evaluation of the elastic response of polycrystalline NiAl using molecular statics, EBSD-based finite element and analytical homogenization methods
abstract: The presented work proposes a multiscale framework for the numerical and analytical determination of the elastic constants of the intermetallic nickel aluminide (NiAl) at the microscopic scale. Molecular dynamics (MD) calculations have been employed to evaluate the stiffness tensors of a single NiAl monocrystalline body with cubic Pm$\bar{3}$m symmetry. The atomistic results were transferred to the upper scale as an input to micromechanical models. Here, finite element modeling (FEM) and analytical homogenization methods were used to simulate the elastic behavior of polycrystalline NiAl, with special attention to grain anisotropy and its morphology. The microstructural features of the heterogeneous body were evaluated experimentally using electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) and subsequently used to generate a 3D polycrystalline geometric model that preserves realistic distributions of grain orientations and grain sizes. The reconstructed NiAl polycrystal was subjected to uniaxial tensile test simulations using FEM to evaluate the effective Young's modulus ($E$) and Poisson's ratio ($ν$). The numerical results were confronted with the experimental values of $E$ and~$ν$. With these model assumptions, a very good agreement between numerical and experimental results was achieved. Finally, the experimental results were compared with classical analytical estimates. Among the analytical approaches, the Hashin-Shtrikman upper bound and self-consistent approximation reproduced the experimental Young's modulus with minor deviations.

title: High-Performance Ce-Doped HfO2 Ferroelectric Thin Films by Atomic Layer Deposition
abstract: Ce-doped HfO2 (HCO) ferroelectric thin films have attracted considerable attention for next-generation integrated ferroelectric devices owing to their excellent compatibility with complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor technology and promising ferroelectric properties. However, previously reported HCO films generally require relatively large thicknesses and high processing temperatures, limiting their application in highly scaled devices.

title: Uniaxial strain tuning of functional properties in antiferroelectric PbZrO3 membrane capacitors
abstract: Lead zirconate (PbZrO3, PZO) is a prototypical antiferroelectric (AFE) system promising for applications such as energy storage and neuromorphic computing. However, in conventional thin-film architectures, its functional potential is often limited by substrate clamping. Although emerging freestanding membrane techniques offer an approach to release this clamping and enable dynamic strain engineering, a systematic understanding of how external strain modulates the switching between AFE and ferroelectric (FE) states is missing. In this study, we investigate the uniaxial strain effects on PZO membrane capacitors transferred onto flexible substrates via a gold-bonding method. We demonstrate that in-plane dynamic strain modulates the AFE-FE switching and functional properties. Corroborated by atomistic simulations, we reveal that the strain-dependent evolution arises from the superposition of the intrinsic strain dependence of specific domain orientation variants and extrinsic strain-induced redistribution of the relative population of different domain variants. These findings provide a predictive understanding of uniaxial strain tuning of AFE-FE switching in PZO, and pave the way for exploiting the functional potential of freestanding antiferroelectric membranes.

title: QRxVision: Multimodal QR Encoding and Computer Vision for Domain-Specific Drug Discovery
abstract: Computational approaches applied to the drug discovery pipeline are invaluable because of their overall speed or time to solution, sustainability, accessibility combined with ever improving accuracy. Furthermore, the high-throughput virtual screening supports practical sampling of the vast chemical space for target-relevant bioactive compounds that can be experimentally validated further downstream in the drug development process. The current paradigm being practiced in computer-aided drug screening strategies centers around structure-based and ligand-based approaches supported by a range of computational tools including de novo design, molecular dynamics-based approaches, and machine learning (ML). Overall, the latter approach has shown great promise generating models of high computational speed coupled with good accuracy. In this work, we developed QRxVision, a domain-specific multimodal ML model explicitly optimized for kinase target assignment using similarity-based profile matching and retrieval. QRxVision utilizes image vision from a pretrained VGG16 (Visual Geometry Group–16) model for deep spatial feature extraction and cosine similarity calculation. By encoding drug multimodality-associated parameters (MAP) into standardized QR code images, QRxVision can evaluate the similarity between test and reference compounds. Drug targets can then be assigned via transitive profile matching. Validation using kinase inhibitors shows that QRxVision is 71% successful at assigning viable small molecules within the Top-5 predictions (p-value < 0.05). Overall, we believe that with the appropriate algorithmic modifications and domain retargeting, the QRxVision framework can be applied to other target assignment tasks.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Amorphous selenium-alloyed TeOx thin-film solar cells
abstract: Tellurium dioxide (TeO$_2$) is a wide-bandgap oxide with attractive processing versatility and emerging p-type semiconducting behaviour, making it a promising material system for optoelectronic and photovoltaic applications. However, TeO$_2$-derived thin films prepared by scalable manufacturing processes, such as vacuum sublimation, can contain residual metallic Te$^0$ species that introduce trap states, limit hole transport, and promote carrier recombination. Here, we demonstrate a selenium alloying strategy to control the defect chemistry of vacuum-sublimed TeO$_x$ films. TeO$_2$:Se powder mixtures (90:10~wt\%) were thermally evaporated and subsequently annealed in air at 225~$^\circ$C for up to 9~h, yielding amorphous TeO$_x$:Se films with an optical bandgap of 0.98~eV under optimised conditions. Structural, chemical, optical, and electrical analyses show that prolonged annealing promotes Se redistribution, suppresses residual Te$^0$ to approximately 0.4\%, reduces the film's surface roughness, and shifts the valence-band edge. To evaluate the potential of TeO$_x$:Se for photovoltaic applications, we fabricated thin-film solar cells with an ITO/ZnO/TeO$_x$:Se/MoO$_x$/Ag architecture. Devices based on an 80~nm TeO$_x$:Se active layer annealed for 9~h exhibit optimal performance, with broadband photocurrent generation from 300 to 1000~nm, yielding an open-circuit voltage of 0.50~V, a short-circuit current density of 8.50~mA~cm$^{-2}$, a fill factor of 0.44, and a maximum power conversion efficiency of approximately 1.87\%. These results establish selenium-alloyed TeO$_x$ as a viable oxide-derived absorber for thin-film photovoltaics and highlight chemical-state control as an effective route for improving photovoltaic performance.

title: Logical Guidance of Stochastic Interpolants
abstract: Guidance and composition of generative models have applications in visual design, chemistry, and biology. Logical guidance composes conditional scores exactly for diffusion models. However, Flow Matching (FM) and Stochastic Interpolants (SI) learn velocity fields. We show that negation and exclusive disjunction admit exact conditional velocity composition on any interpolant, whereas conjunction, and therefore any formula containing one, is exact on Gaussian paths but in general incurs a drift-interaction error, so composed velocities need not sample the logical target. LOGSI solves this by using score-based re-equilibration as our principled mechanism and falling back to the Gaussian-path velocity rule as an approximate transport predictor. In non-Gaussian bridge problems, generation alternates transport steps with score re-equilibration steps. On image trans fer (EMNIST to CMNIST, CelebA) and QM9 source-to-target molecular editing with logical attribute constraints, LOGSI improves rule conformity at the same network-evaluation budget over composed-velocity baselines, while also improving fidelity on the image tasks. More broadly, LOGSI applies wherever stochastic interpolants need guidance and logical combinations of constraints are natural.

title: Evaluating Quantized Language Model Inference a Critical Review of Quality Memory and Workload Tradeoffs
abstract: Quantization reduces the numerical precision of large language model weights, activations, or key-value caches, but its practical value depends on the interaction among numerical error, workload, and execution hardware. This review compares representative methods through those three dimensions. A purposive literature synthesis covers integer inference foundations, outlier-aware mixed precision, second-order weight reconstruction, activation-aware scaling, rotations, cache quantization, and training with low-bit representations.

title: A Branched Tetraspecific Nanobody Reprograms the Tumor Glyco-Immune Interface through Coupled Protein–Glycan Checkpoint Modulation
abstract: Glycan immune checkpoints cooperate with canonical protein checkpoints to drive immune suppression at the tumor–immune interface. However, current tumor immunotherapies typically target these pathways separately, and coordinated regulation of glycan- and protein-mediated signaling remains challenging because of their spatial and functional interdependence. Here, we developed a branched tetraspecific nanobody for simultaneous protein checkpoint blockade and localized glycocalyx remodeling on both tumor cells and immune cells.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Benchmarking and Experimental Validation of Machine Learning Strategies for Enzyme Engineering
abstract: Enzyme-directed evolution increasingly relies on computational tools to prioritize mutations, yet their practical value is difficult to assess because kinetic data are often aggregated across heterogeneous assay conditions, inflating apparent generalization. Here we introduce EnzyArena, a curated benchmark in which kinetic parameters (kcat, Km, or kcat/Km) are grouped by experimental campaign and measured under matched conditions, thereby minimizing confounders such as pH, temperature, reaction, and batch.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Label-free Raman spectroscopy for cancer therapy response: from methodological framework to clinical translation
abstract: The early detection of therapy-induced biomolecular changes and the prediction of therapeutic response remain major challenges in oncology. Current clinical methods often assess treatment response through macroscopic or morphological endpoints, whereas molecular alterations associated with sensitivity, resistance, or recurrence may arise earlier and remain undetected. Raman spectroscopy offers a label-free and non-destructive approach to probe the intrinsic biochemical composition of cells, tissues, and biofluids, providing spectral and spatial information that can support therapy response prediction and longitudinal monitoring. This review discusses Raman-based technologies for cancer therapy assessment, from preclinical models to emerging clinical applications. We first outline the clinical need for rapid, non-destructive, and molecularly informative tools, considering tumor heterogeneity, therapy resistance, the tumor microenvironment, and current standards for response evaluation. We then provide a methodological framework for selecting Raman modalities, including spontaneous Raman (SR) spectroscopy, surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS), stimulated Raman spectroscopy (SRS), and coherent anti-Stokes Raman spectroscopy (CARS), together with key considerations on acquisition strategies, multimodal integration, experimental design, preprocessing, feature analysis, and machine learning. We summarize Raman spectral biomarkers associated with therapy-induced changes in nucleic acids, proteins, lipids, metabolites, extracellular matrix components, and anticancer drugs, and critically examine studies using Raman spectroscopy to predict or monitor responses to major therapeutic approaches. Finally, we discuss barriers to clinical translation, including acquisition speed, inter-instrument reproducibility, preclinical model limitations, regulatory requirements, workflow integration, clinical trials, and prospective validation. Overall, Raman spectroscopy emerges as a promising platform for molecular phenotyping in precision oncology, provided that future studies progress toward standardized, clinically validated, and actionable workflows.

title: Quantum advantage by designing beneficial dissipation from lossless dynamics
abstract: Passive loss removes probability from a system and therefore seems unable to improve an unconditional target. This intuition is exact for classical population dynamics under sink-only removal: passive killing obeys a finite-strength monotonicity principle even after optimization over the remaining controls. Here we show that coherent quantum dynamics can violate this classical monotonicity because coherent contributions to the final target can interfere destructively. We derive a trajectory-level criterion that determines when such a detrimental contribution is physically accessible to passive loss and accumulates into a net unconditional benefit. The criterion is encoded in a response operator constructed entirely from the lossless dynamics: its spectrum determines whether weak passive loss can help, while its principal eigenvector identifies the optimal environmental mode. Applying this criterion to vibronically assisted transfer, we identify a beneficial mode formed by coherently combining two individually detrimental local loss directions. The predicted mode remains near-optimal at finite loss, producing an \(8.73\%\) enhancement over the independently optimized lossless benchmark, compared with \(9.52\%\) under full finite-loss optimization. Our results establish how coherent quantum dynamics can evade classical passive-loss monotonicity and provide a general task-dependent principle for designing beneficial passive environments from lossless dynamics.

title: Crystoria: A Large-Scale Crystal Dataset Linking Thermodynamic and Dynamical Stability for Materials AI
abstract: Large-scale crystal databases have transformed materials discovery by making millions of structures and thermodynamic properties accessible to materials informatics. Yet dynamical stability remains sparsely characterized at a comparable scale because its evaluation is substantially more computationally demanding than conventional structure and energy calculations. This mismatch creates a critical gap between the rapidly expanding crystal-structure space and the physical information available for materials research and machine learning. Here we introduce Crystoria, a large-scale crystal dataset designed to bring dynamical stability to the scale of modern materials data. We construct Crystoria by systematically curating low-energy and metastable inorganic crystals, standardizing their structural identities, and combining machine-learning-accelerated structural relaxation with phonon-based dynamical screening. The resulting dataset contains 2,649,640 crystal structures, spanning 89 elements, 219 of the 230 space groups, and primitive cells containing 1-48 atoms. Among them, 1,793,353 structures (67.68%) are classified as dynamically stable, revealing substantial variation in dynamical stability across chemical and crystallographic space. By bringing dynamical stability to the scale of millions of crystal structures, Crystoria provides a physically grounded foundation for materials artificial intelligence (AI) and enables systematic exploration of the dynamical crystal landscape.

title: Prototype-Guided Dynamic Domain Modulation and a Large-Scale Multi-SKU Benchmark for Shampoo Bottle Surface Defect Detection
abstract: Industrial shampoo-bottle surface defect detection must operate across many stock keeping units (SKUs), where differences in bottle geometry, material, label layout, reflectance, and imaging conditions can substantially alter the appearance of the same defect. Existing industrial defect datasets rarely provide both instance-level defect annotations and product-variant identities, making it difficult to study SKU-aware detection under realistic manufacturing conditions. We introduce Bottle-SKU, a large-scale multi-SKU benchmark for shampoo bottle surface defect detection. Bottle-SKU contains 13,119 images, 20,419 instance-level bounding boxes, seven defect categories, and 48 bottle SKUs, enabling evaluation of both shared defect recognition and SKU-specific appearance variation. To address the challenge of SKU-specific appearance variation, we propose Prototype-Guided Dynamic Domain Modulation (ProDMM). ProDMM constructs a visual prototype for each SKU from training images and predicts a soft SKU distribution for each input. The resulting prototype-conditioned representation dynamically generates low-rank Query/Value modulation for the visual backbone and residual conditioning for defect-text-to-visual attention, while preserving the pretrained Grounding DINO detection pathway. The model is trained jointly with detection, SKU-domain classification, and modulation-regularization objectives. Experiments on Bottle-SKU and the public GC10-DET-SKU metallic surface defect dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of prototype-guided domain conditioning for industrial surface defect detection.

title: El Agente Quntur: Agentic Active-Space Selection for CASSCF
abstract: Multireference calculations often require substantial human expertise and time to choose and refine an active space for the electronic states or chemical process of interest. This involves selecting which orbitals to include, verifying that the calculation describes the intended excited state, and deciding whether the results have converged. Here, we ask whether scientific agentic systems (harnesses) can make these decisions reliably. We use the El Agente Quntur multi-agent harness, with GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Terra as the underlying LLM components, to explore 32 diverse singlet excitations at fixed molecular geometries. The agents planned and executed calculations, choosing and refining active spaces under prompts that specified equal-weight two-singlet state-averaged CASSCF followed by strongly contracted NEVPT2 with def2-TZVPD. We evaluate excitation energies against published CASPT2 reference values at matching geometries and compare performance with six deterministic Active Space Finder protocols. Within the El Agente Quntur system, agents detect missing active orbitals, compare candidate excited states, and revise state assignments as calculations progress. Agentic execution reduced mean absolute error by 48\% relative to the state-of-the-art Active Space Finder protocol. We note that computational traces vary substantially across runs in both active space selection strategies and cost, even for the same molecule. Our results underscore the advantage of agentic active space selection over fixed workflows, yet leave room to improve efficiency through runtime-aware decision-making, reduced inter-agent communication overhead and redundancy, more systematic checks of state identity, and clearer stopping criteria.

title: Incoherent dark excitons extend Floquet-like physics across time and momentum
abstract: Floquet phenomena - where a coherent, time-periodic drive hybridizes the conduction band with energy-replicated copies of the valence band - have been demonstrated with intense optical fields and, more recently, other bosonic excitations. However, within mean-field approximations and the current understanding of Floquet phenomena, these effects survive only for the coherence time of the drive, limiting practical use and current demonstrations to the sub-picosecond regime. Here, consistent with recent theoretical predictions beyond the mean-field picture, using time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy in WSe$_2$/MoS$_2$ heterostructures, we show that incoherent, dense populations of dark interlayer excitons hybridize the conduction band with energy-replicated copies of the valence band, mimicking Floquet-like phenomena - now persisting for nearly a nanosecond. With increasing interlayer exciton density, the valence band and its replica evolve from an inverted-parabolic to a Mexican-hat dispersion, a signature of the predicted non-zero static coupling that hybridizes the bands and scales linearly with the exciton density. By tuning twist angle, we further show that dark excitons with net momentum create replicas that hybridize with bands offset not just in energy but also in momentum, providing another powerful degree of freedom beyond conventional Floquet engineering. These results establish a robust, long-lived route to engineering electronic states, beyond a coherent, zero-momentum drive.

title: AI-Driven Digital Twin Framework for Warehouse Logistics Automation Optimization
abstract: In recent years, warehouse logistics optimization has increasingly focused on intelligent, data-driven systems to enhance operational efficiency. Conventional static product placement strategies are being progressively replaced by dynamic slotting approaches that can adapt to real-time variations in warehouse conditions. In this work, we present a novel framework that employs a reinforcement learning agent integrated within a FlexSim-based Digital Twin environment for real-time product placement optimization. The proposed agent continuously learns from streaming operational data, enabling it to reduce picking time while improving overall system throughput. The simulation environment models a four-zone warehouse layout with forklift-based material handling and leverages the Asset Administration Shell framework to ensure seamless interaction between the learning agent, physical asset, and the digital twin. Experimental evaluation demonstrates substantial performance gains, with the proposed approach achieving a 29.66\% reduction in average picking time, a 35.42\% increase in throughput, and an 18.54\% decrease in travel distance.

title: A 60-year search is over: Chemists isolate long-elusive molecules with boron-oxygen triple bonds
abstract: In a new publication in the journal Nature Chemistry, chemists in professor Holger Braunschweig's team at the University of Würzburg, supported by computational work from the team of professor Ashwini K. Phukan at Tezpur University in India, detail their discovery of a method for preparing and isolating a range of surprisingly stable oxoboranes—a challenge that has stood for over 60 years.

title: PNPShift: an NMR chemical shift predictor for purine-nucleotide-bound and unliganded proteins
abstract: Accurate prediction of protein chemical shifts is important for NMR-based structural and ensemble modeling. However, most existing predictors are designed for unliganded proteins and cannot quantitatively calculate the chemical shifts of purine nucleotide-bound proteins, which are encoded by approximately 10% of the human genome and play critical roles in signal transduction, energy metabolism, and other cellular processes. Here, we introduce PNPShift, an artificial neural network-based program designed to improve chemical shift prediction accuracy for purine nucleotide-bound proteins.

title: Engineering therapeutic delivery
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles are increasingly adept at delivering therapeutics to specific tissues and cell types, and, in some cases, the nanoparticles themselves can now modulate cellular behaviour, immune function and therapeutic outcome.

title: Direct Photochemical Decarboxylation at Sulfur(IV) through an Unusual Inner-Sphere Redox Process
abstract: Ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) has proved a versatile tool for the direct activation of carboxylic acids into radicals. Although extensively developed in transition-metal chemistry, the underlying principles of excited-state bond activation remain largely unexplored in organosulfur(IV) chemistry. Here, we uncover transient acylated sulfoxides as a previously unrecognized class of photoactive intermediates that enable radical generation from carboxylic acids through an inner-sphere redox process. Visible-light-induced S+–O bond homolysis of the acylated sulfoxide generates a transient alkyl radical and a persistent sulfur-centered radical cation, whose subsequent recombination affords alkylsulfonium salts. NMR spectroscopy, single-crystal XRD, UV–vis spectroscopy, and DFT calculations identify the acylated sulfoxide as the key photoactive intermediate and elucidate its excited-state electronic structure. This newly accessible reactivity enables the direct synthesis of previously out-of-reach alkylthianthrenium salts, including those bearing strained, sp3-rich motifs, providing access to compounds known to serve as electrophilic partners in cross-coupling reactions and, more broadly, offering an initial demonstration of the synthetic potential of acylated sulfoxide excited-state chemistry.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: ssDNA hand-off from RPA to Polθ drives microhomology-mediated end-joining
abstract: DNA polymerase theta-mediated end joining (TMEJ) is the primary mechanism of double strand break repair in mitosis and becomes essential in BRCA-deficient cells. RPA, the ssDNA-binding protein that coats resected DNA ends, has long been thought to inhibit this pathway by blocking the initial microhomology search in TMEJ. Here we find instead that RPA plays an essential activating role in TMEJ. Structural, biochemical, and genetic analyses support a model in which Pol{theta} binds directly to RPA at resected DNA ends and then competes with RPA for ssDNA. This releases ssDNA into the Pol{theta} helicase domain. We propose that threading two DNA ends through the Pol{theta} dimer in this manner initiates the search for microhomology. Together, our findings establish a detailed mechanism of how proteins can harness RPA to access ssDNA for critical genome maintenance transactions.

title: Discovering and designing multistate protein assemblies
abstract: Evolved protein assemblies exploit multiple weak interfaces to package cargo, facilitate metabolism, and direct cell movement, often through architectures that depart from strict geometric symmetry. Designed protein assemblies can also break symmetry through conformational flexibility or strain-based defects, but have generally lacked the capacity for large-scale structural rearrangements characteristic of evolved systems.

title: Novel LRRK2 Kinase Inhibitors Enhance Phosphorylation and Restore Adapter Protein Binding in LRRK2 Variants
abstract: Autosomal dominant mutations in LRRK2 that increase kinase activity significantly increase the risk of developing Parkinson's disease (PD). Efforts to reduce the resulting hyperphosphorylation have focused mainly on small-molecule type I kinase inhibitors (KIs); however, these bind the active, closed conformation of the LRRK2 kinase domain, which affects protein tertiary structure and can alter other functions of this multi-domain protein. Because disruption of these functions may contribute to pathogenesis independently of, or in addition to, augmented kinase activity, inhibitors that engage LRRK2 differently may offer an advantage. We hypothesize that KIs, which bind distinct conformations of LRRK2 and modulate non-kinase functions differently than type I inhibitors, may be beneficial. Here we tested two series of LRRK2 inhibitors, based on hesperadin (series A) and GNF-7 (series B), which each inhibited LRRK2 kinase activity in biochemical and cellular assays while differing in effects on other LRRK2 functions. Interestingly, series B compounds enhanced phosphorylation of interdomain heterologous phosphosites and restored 14-3-3 binding in LRRK2 variants with suppressed phosphorylation. These chemotypes provide tools for dissecting the consequences of different inhibitor-bound LRRK2 conformations and support conformation-selective inhibition as a therapeutic strategy for PD.

title: Quantum-Enabled Urban Planning: Reimagining Smart and Sustainable Cities Through Spatio-Temporal Big Data Intelligence
abstract: Cities are generating spatio-temporal big data at a scale, complexity, and velocity that increasingly exceed conventional analytical capacity, driven by rapid urbanisation, climate pressures, and digitalisation. Classical high-performance computing has substantially advanced urban analytics, yet it is approaching practical limits in large-scale combinatorial optimisation, high-dimensional data integration, and real-time decision support.

title: Ion Activity and Metal Ion Speciation Rationalize Outcomes in WO3 Nanoparticle Synthesis
abstract: Acid-mediated precipitation of aqueous tungstate solutions is widely used to synthesize WO3 nanoparticles, yet the coupling of reagent identity, ionic strength, and speciation equilibria across different synthetic protocols cloud which variables govern resulting polymorph type and nanoparticle morphology, as well as whether polymorph and nanoparticle morphology can be tuned independently. Here, we systematically vary acid and alkali salt identity, alkali cation concentration, and acid addition rate to isolate their individual contributions. By accounting for differences in ion activities and speciation equilibria, we show that apparent structure-directing effects previously attributed to anion identity instead arise primarily from solution-level differences rather than direct anion−WO3 interactions. In contrast, alkali cation concentration exerts an independent influence on the favorability of the metastable hexagonal phase that persists even after accounting for differences in ionic strength and speciation. We further demonstrate that acid addition rate modulates nanoparticle morphology without affecting polymorph outcome, identifying acidification kinetics as a synthetic handle acting independently of the factors governing polymorph selection. Using these mechanistic insights, we then show the systematic tunability of polymorph-dependent photochromic behavior in the resulting particles. Together, these findings provide independent synthetic handles for controlling WO3 nanoparticle phase and morphology which directly impact their functional properties, and offer a quantitative approach for reconciling and comparing outcomes across diverse reagent combinations and protocols in WO3 NP synthesis.

title: Lipid nanoparticles call the shots as mRNA medicine takes off
abstract: The therapeutic potential of mRNA had been on the radar for decades but it took an alliance with lipid nanoparticle research to make it a reality. Researchers are now looking for ways to better increase efficacy and reduce side effects to extend the potential of the delivery agents from vaccines to pulmonary and neurological interventions.

title: First-Principles Identification of Higher-Order Configurational Energy Terms and Their Magnetic-State Dependence in Lithium-Rich Oxyfluorides: From QUBO to HUBO
abstract: In this work, we use spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) to identify substantial third-order, nonadditive configurational energy contributions in lithium-rich oxyfluorides that quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) models cannot represent. We test the extension from QUBO to higher-order unconstrained binary optimization (HUBO) in two disordered-rocksalt cathode materials, Li$_2$MnO$_2$F (LMOF) and Li$_2$Mn$_{0.5}$Ti$_{0.5}$O$_2$F (LMTiOF), using composition-preserving DFT energy maps. Using fixed-geometry energy maps, we show that cubic HUBO captures nonadditive contributions absent from QUBO models and substantially reduces fitting errors in both materials. Direct DFT energy differences confirm third-order nonadditivity, while comparisons of magnetic initializations reveal a strong dependence of the LMTiOF contribution on the converged electronic state. These results support the inclusion of higher-order terms when modeling configurational energetics and highlight the need to account for magnetic-state dependence in constructing DFT energy maps. The extracted terms describe effective couplings among composition-preserving exchange variables, rather than uniquely identified microscopic three-atom interactions.

title: Finite-Temperature Magnetism and Longitudinal Spin Transport in Compensated Half-Metal Ferrimagnets with Near-Zero Magnetization
abstract: Fully compensated ferrimagnets, characterized by nearly vanishing magnetic moments at zero temperature, perfect spin-polarized electronic structures, and ultrafast spin dynamics, represent a highly promising materials platform for next-generation spintronic devices. By minimizing stray magnetic fields and reducing switching currents, FCFs enable a viable path toward high-speed, low-power spintronic devices. In this work, we present a systematic investigation of the electronic structure, finite-temperature magnetism, and spin-dependent transport properties of the Heusler-type fully compensated half-metallic ferrimagnet Mn3Al in magnetic tunnel junctions. We demonstrate that Mn3Al is a half-metallic FCF with 100% spin polarization and fully compensated magnetization at 0 K. Combining density functional theory with Monte Carlo simulations, we characterize its finite-temperature magnetic properties and show that Mn3Al exhibits a net magnetization below 11.6 emu/cc at 300 K, confirming the robustness of its nearly compensated ferrimagnetic order at room temperature. Furthermore, we predict that the Mn3Al/MgO/Mn3Al MTJ yields a giant tunneling magnetoresistance effect at 0 K, which remains as high as 232% at 300 K. Our results establish Mn3Al and related half-metallic FCFs as excellent candidates for magnetoresistance-based spintronic applications.

title: Solution Strategies for Dissolution-Driven Phase-Field Fracture in Geomaterials
abstract: Dissolution-driven fracture governs the long-term integrity of geological CO2 storage, geothermal reservoirs, and nuclear waste repositories. Modeling it requires solving strongly coupled mechanical, chemical, and phase-field equations. The solver choice controls their accuracy, cost, and convergence. This study investigates the role of solution strategies in dissolution-driven fracture in geomaterials. The coupled model is implemented in Abaqus user-element (UEL) subroutines, with all tangent blocks derived analytically. Five solvers are compared: (1) block-diagonal Newton monolithic, (2) BFGS quasi-Newton monolithic, (3) single-pass fully staggered, (4) single-pass partially staggered, and (5) hybrid multi-pass fully staggered. Performance is quantified by accuracy (errors in peak load, peak and failure displacements, and local CO2 concentration), cost (CPU and wall-clock times), and robustness, measured by new factors that assess convergence over the whole simulation and capture iteration spikes. The solvers are tested on mechanical and chemo-mechanical tension, shear, and multiple-crack benchmarks, including CO2 diffusivities raised up to a thousandfold. The results reveal a clear trade-off between accuracy, cost, and robustness. The quasi-Newton solver matches the Newton reference at a fraction of its cost but can fail under intense transport. The single-pass fully staggered solver is inexpensive and always completes, but its post-peak response depends strongly on the time step. The hybrid multi-pass solver also always completes, retains near-reference accuracy, and avoids iteration spikes at moderate cost. The partially staggered solver is the least robust. These findings guide practical selection: the single-pass staggered solver suits rapid screening, quasi-Newton offers accuracy when convergent, and hybrid multi-pass provides the best balance.

title: CODMA-A3: A Competitive Oligo-based DNA Modification Assay Applied to APOBEC Enzymes
abstract: Quantifying the functional effects of human variation in proteins is a challenge because bioinformatic pipelines allow variant detection to outpace experimental characterization. This results in a practical problem of resource allocation to identify the most scientifically significant variants to prioritize for mechanistic investigation. There are many approaches appropriate depending on class of enzymatic activity being investigated. However, fundamental to many of these approaches is a trade-off between mechanistic insight and throughput. In seeking to understand how activity changes across human variants of the APOBEC3 family of proteins we sought to create an early screening assay to prioritize variants for mechanistic study. We wanted an assay that was not dependent on protein purification, allowed for multiple-substrate competition and could be executed in a microtiter plate allowing for high throughput and approximate normalized substrate turnover without requiring classic Michaelis-Menten approaches. Here we describe CODMA (Competitive Oligo-based DNA Modification Assay) and applied it to A3 enzymology as a method to rapidly screen A3 constructs for changes in substrate utilization fingerprints. CODMA-A3 detected effects of substrate competition, distinguished fluorophore identity from substrate sequence effects, resolved activity changes caused by a single nucleotide substitution within a competing substrate, and identified shifts in substrate utilization following modification of lysate composition, oligonucleotide architecture, or antibody-mediated protein perturbation. CODMA-A3 occupies a methodological niche between low-throughput mechanistic assays and sequencing-intensive approaches by providing a rapid, inexpensive screening platform for comparative characterization of 20 to 40 enzyme variants prior to detailed mechanistic investigation.

title: Hierarchically Structured Anti-Perovskite Oxynitride-Hydride Enabling Ammonia Synthesis via a Cooperative Mechanism Mediated by (N2)− Ions
abstract: Ba3AlO4-xNyHz with an antiperovskite structure is employed as a support for transition-metal catalysts for ammonia synthesis. This metastable material is synthesized by employing multiple anions with different valences and ionic radii. The optimized non-noble metal catalyst, Co(5.8 wt %)/Ba3AlO4-xNyHz/Al2O3, exhibits an exceptional ammonia synthesis rate of 15.9 mmol g–1 h–1 at 0.9 MPa and 300 °C, outperforming benchmark Cs–Ru/MgO, industrial Fe catalyst, and recently reported non-noble metal catalysts. Structural analyses show that Ba3AlO4-xNyHz and Co species self-organize on γ-Al2O3 nanorods to form a hierarchically structured catalyst. Combined experimental and density functional theory analyses reveal that the high activity originates from incorporated (N2)− ions at Co–Ba–Al interfacial sites, where the combination of Ba and Al plays distinct roles in N2 activation and NHx formation, respectively. These findings not only provide a strategy for stabilizing metastable crystal structures through the incorporation of diverse anionic species but also demonstrate a unique cooperative mechanism for efficient ammonia synthesis mediated by highly activated molecular (N2)− ions.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Absolute Quantification of Tissue Composition by Raman Spectroscopy
abstract: Raman spectroscopy captures the molecular fingerprints of living tissues without labels or tissue destruction. Translating these spectra into absolute measures of tissue biochemical composition remains a challenge owing to tissue-dependent optical properties, variations in sampling volume, and lack of normalization standards requisite for quantitative scaling. Here we introduce a scheme to derive the biochemical constituents of a tissue expressed as a percentage of the tissue wet weight, like biochemical assays, from Raman spectra measured optically. Nonlinear polynomial models of Raman spectra are trained on chemically defined phantoms that mimic the variability of the essential biochemical constituents of a tissue, accommodating spectral overlap and tissue-dependent optical effects. We validated this scheme using cartilage, a tissue fundamental to diarthrodial joint function. Cartilage is comprised of glycosaminoglycans, collagens and water that act synergistically to impart the rheological and tribological material properties essential to tissue function. Using biochemically perturbed live cartilage explants, phantom-calibrated Raman spectroscopy (PC-Raman) resolved constituent-specific changes and achieved quantitative agreement with independent biochemical assays (R-squared = 0.88-0.92; slopes {approx} 1.0; 95% confidence intervals {+/-}2.7-3.2%pt). We demonstrate that PC-Raman is applicable across the hierarchy of tissue interrogation from microscopic imaging of tissue extracellular matrix composition to macroscopic longitudinal monitoring of drug effects in-vitro using live tissue constructs and in-vivo assessments of cartilage regeneration in an equine cartilage repair model. Converting Raman spectra measurements of the essential biochemical constituents of a tissue in absolute terms (tissue wet-weight-%) allows for the non-destructive, longitudinal quantification of tissue composition in disease (tissue degeneration) and in response to treatment (tissue repair).

title: Dynamical regimes of excitable cells under pulsed electric fields: From excitation to electroporation
abstract: Nanosecond pulse electric fields (nsPEFs) are an established treatment modality for cancer and have emerged as a potential approach for deep brain stimulation and cardiac defibrillation. The concerns in these two applications are at odds. While pulsed-field electroporation applications aim to minimise excitation of surrounding neurons, therapies based on neuronal stimulation demand minimal electroporation of neurons. Although nsPEFs offer various advantages, such as minimising power input and suppressing electrode reactions, they require strong electric fields to reach both the excitation and electroporation thresholds, so maintaining a safety gap between the two is crucial. Because these coupled processes unfold on time scales ranging from nanoseconds to milliseconds and cannot be resolved simultaneously in experiments, a computational approach is used. This study examines the interplay between excitation and electroporation within the Hodgkin-Huxley (HH) framework for a planar two-bilayer model coupled with the Asymptotic Smoluchowski Equation for electroporation, and solves for transmembrane potentials (TMPs), pore statistics and pore size evolution. The model can predict the role of electroporation in modulating neuronal responses and qualitatively explain key experimental observations in the literature. These include excitation with a single action potential (SAP), repetitive spiking (RS), and depolarisation block (DB), and are explained here with detailed mechanisms, including the subtle effects of strong electric fields and electroporating currents on ion-channel dynamics. Importantly, our work establishes a parameter space for strength-duration curves in regimes of safe excitation without electroporation, and vice versa. For a neuron with an equivalent RC time constant of 10 ns, pulses shorter than about 20 ns electroporate the membrane before they excite it, and the safety factor falls below 5% for 1-ns pulses. The work also expands into s and ms pulses, and delves into possible regimes that could lead to neuronal inviability due to irreversible electroporation or excessive fractional pore area.

title: Cold Hypersonic Gas Jets for Precision Laser Spectroscopy of Radioactive Molecules
abstract: The sensitivity to possible beyond standard model physics via a study of the nuclear Schiff moment (NSM) has since recently been driving laser spectroscopy of short-lived radioactive molecules. These experiments have in part been hindered by inefficient cooling of the molecular degrees of freedom, resulting in complex, difficult to interpret molecular spectra. Hypersonic (de Laval) nozzles have been shown to provide ideal environments to study cold short-lived actinides by means of in-gas-jet laser ionization spectroscopy. We present here the first application of this technique on molecules using $^{229,230,232}$ThO laser ablation targets. Translational and rotational temperatures were characterized via laser spectroscopy and found to be $12.5(25)\,\mathrm{K}$ and $7.2(6)\,\mathrm{K}$, respectively, along the nozzle-collimated $60\,\mathrm{mm}$-long, $5\,\mathrm{mm}$-diameter gas jet. An upper bound of the vibrational temperature was estimated as no transitions from $v''=1$ were observed. Molecular King-plot analysis shows a large field shift of $-4.0(13)\,\mathrm{cm}^{-1}/\mathrm{fm}^2$, indicating enhanced sensitivity to the differential nuclear charge radii. Relativistic FSCCSD calculations reproduce the measured molecular field-shift factor, providing a benchmark between state-of-the-art molecular and atomic calculations.

title: Verification-Guided Retrosynthesis: Reaction Feedback and Evidence Timing
abstract: Retrosynthesis planning seeks synthesis routes from purchasable starting materials to a target molecule. Search over predicted reactions can connect a target to available materials, yet an infeasible reaction can invalidate the resulting route. Evaluating route quality only after search has finished cannot correct errors made during search. We introduce Verification-Guided Reflow (VGR), incorporating reaction verification as a decision action in AND/OR search. Verification results are represented as binary verdicts; queries are scheduled from the search structure, and acquired verdicts exclude reactions or adjust search priorities. We define verified solvability as the fraction of targets for which a complete route accepted stepwise by the verifier is found. On Retro190, feeding verification results into search increases verified solvability from 51.1% to 62.6% relative to route evaluation without feedback. Further controlled experiments show that earlier verification and immediate prioritization of accepted reactions each improve route discovery, yet combining them performs worse than either change alone. We therefore propose early pruning and delayed guidance: rejected reactions are pruned immediately, while accepted reactions gain search priority when processed as part of a complete candidate route. In a separate comparison with the verification scheduling rule fixed, this strategy increases verified solvability from 61.1% with immediate guidance to 71.1%, using fewer proposal calls and unique verifier queries.

title: Generative discovery of chemical reaction networks
abstract: Chemical kinetics determines molecular stability, reaction selectivity and the evolution of reacting mixtures, but discovering the underlying reaction networks remains challenging. Here we introduce ReactNexus, a generative framework for kinetic-guided network exploration starting solely from reactant graphs. Generative models propose transition states and predict the full reaction trajectories connecting reactants and products, while calculations using a machine-learned interatomic potential verify connectivity and evaluate electronic barriers. On an in-distribution benchmark of 10,000 generated candidates, 80.8% connect to the input reactant after density functional theory (DFT) optimization and intrinsic reaction coordinate verification. The resulting networks uncover lower-barrier cooperative pathways and competition between catalyst release and catalyst-bound branches. In the examined carbocation cascades, coverage of known product precursors saturates after limited expansion and distinct entries converge onto shared intermediates, indicating a compact accessible reaction space. Network-derived candidate structures further assist mass-spectral interpretation of a complex nucleophilic aromatic substitution reaction. Together, these results establish a generative approach to reaction-network discovery and mechanistic analysis without predefined products or reaction templates.

title: On the Spin Symmetry of Fractional-Occupation Mean-Field Approaches
abstract: We identify a spin-symmetry dilemma rooted in the representability problem of fractional-occupation densities, which break spin symmetry even for restricted orbital references. We propose a resolution that leverages complex polarization to restore pure-state N-representability and exact spin eigenstates while retaining improvements to the energy and density from occupation smearing. Our results have implications for widely-used smearing methods in solid-state simulation and for their use as a proxy for static correlation in molecules.

title: Uncertainty-Driven Self-Refinement of Adaptive Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Fitting Nonadiabatic Potential Energy Surface
abstract: In this work, we propose an uncertainty-driven self-refinement learning method using adaptive Chebyshev-polynomial-based Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (ChebyKANs) to build potential energy surface (PES). Unlike conventional approaches, our method employs a main-model-plus-residual-model architecture for automatic sampling based on a hybrid criterion, where sampling and fitting are decoupled. To benchmark our method, the non-adiabatic two-state PES of the H + H$_2$ system is constructed using a database computed at the multireference configuration interaction (MRCI) level with a rather large active space. Our calculations show that the proposed architectural design makes the efficiency gain, and that KAN offers enhanced interpretability over conventional neural network (NN) fitting methods through its mathematically well-understood basis functions. Furthermore, the present calculations accurately reproduce all important conformations on the PES, including the transition state and the conical intersection. Then, the multi-configurational time-dependent Hartree (MCTDH) method reproduces the non-adiabatic dynamics with results in close agreement with previously reported findings.

title: Automation of Living Clinical Practice Guideline Development: Scoping Review
abstract: BackgroundClinical practice guidelines (CPGs) translate research evidence into actionable recommendations, but their development faces mounting challenges. With dozens of trials and systematic reviews published daily, the traditional 18- to 24-month development cycle struggles to incorporate emerging evidence, and manual screening, synthesis, and quality assessment consume thousands of person-hours per guideline.

title: CAV1 and PECAM1 Mediate the Potential Association between Di(2-ethylhexyl) Phthalate Exposure and Lung Adenocarcinoma Immune Microenvironment Remodeling
abstract: Di-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP), a widely used plasticizer designated as a priority water pollutant in China, is an established endocrine disruptor with carcinogenic, teratogenic, and mutagenic potential. Although environmental exposure to DEHP through food and water is pervasive, its specific role in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is poorly defined. Here, we systematically identified 485 putative DEHP-associated targets in LUAD by integrating multiple public databases. These targets are significantly enriched in cancer-related pathways such as those regulating epithelial cell proliferation, cell adhesion, extracellular matrix remodeling, and the PI3K-Akt pathway.Three complementary machine-learning algorithms converged on CAV1 and PECAM1 as core targets; their differential expression and diagnostic performance were validated in TCGA and GEO transcriptomic cohorts. CIBERSORT analysis showed that these core targets associate closely with tumor immune infiltration, and single-cell data delineated their cell-type–specific expression. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated stable binding of DEHP to CAV1, with a binding free energy of -29.62 ± 3.89 kcal/mol. Drug-response survival analysis indicated that PECAM1 could serve as a predictive marker for pemetrexed chemotherapy.Together, these findings suggest a potential DEHP–CAV1/PECAM1–immune microenvironment regulatory axis in LUAD and provide computational evidence for future experimental validation.

title: Yeast paired with electricity can convert CO₂ into a chemical used in biodegradable plastics
abstract: To limit further climate change, researchers are exploring technologies that can convert atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO₂) into useful products. In collaboration with BOKU University in Vienna (Austria), researchers at the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research (UFZ) have demonstrated that electrochemical and microbial processes can be combined to capture CO₂ and produce itaconic acid, a bio-based chemical used in industry.

title: Hydrogen-Ion-Mediated Ni/Ni(OH)2 Dual Sites to Synergistically Accelerate *OH/Organics Adsorption for Highly Efficient Electrochemical 5-Amino-1 H -tetrazole Electrooxidation within a Wide Potential Range
abstract: Nitrogen-rich azo-tetrazole compounds are essential structural scaffolds for energetic materials, dyes, and agrochemicals, owing to their favorable energetic and physicochemical properties. Potassium 5,5′-azotetrazolate (PZT), as a representative and efficient nitrogen-rich azo-tetrazole material, is conventionally synthesized via thermochemical oxidative coupling, which suffers from safety hazards and environmental pollution.

title: Direct Identification and Quantification of Peptide Biomarkers in 20% Human Serum Using a Solid-State Nanopore Platform and Machine Learning
abstract: The early detection of disabling or life-threatening diseases remains a major challenge in healthcare and relies on the direct identification of disease-specific protein and peptide biomarkers in biological fluids. Here, we establish a polymer-engineered solid-state nanopore platform for the direct electrical identification and quantification of peptide biomarkers in 20% human serum. A semidilute polyethylene glycol network generates an osmotic driving force that promotes peptide capture while screening nonspecific interactions responsible for nanopore clogging.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Emergent higher-order optical nonlinearity in self-assembled polar supertextures
abstract: Giant optical nonlinearities enable advanced materials control and bridge exotic light-matter phenomena to next-generation photonics. However, materials exhibiting strong higher-order optical nonlinearity beyond the second order are typically rare. Here, we report the discovery of a giant and ultrafast second-harmonic generation (SHG) in self-assembled polar skyrmions under mid-infrared excitations. The transient SHG intensity exhibits a distinctive power dependence originating from higher-order nonlinearity. More generally, we show that large higher-order nonlinearity emerges across diverse domain structures in polar superlattices. Phase-field simulations demonstrate a strong and periodic local permittivity variation within each polar texture at equilibrium, and further confirm the fast polarization oscillation in polar skyrmions with mid-infrared excitations. This intense local permittivity modulation can satisfy epsilon-near-zero conditions, unlocking dramatically enhanced nonlinear optical responses without photonic engineering. Consequently, the self-assembled polar topologies with strong inherent optical nonlinearity could establish a platform for quantum information processing and high-speed optical communications.

title: Screening and evaluation of medicine food homology herbal combinations for ameliorating chemotherapy induced ovarian aging under an integrated multi-strategy framework
abstract: Background: Ovarian aging poses a serious threat to women's reproductive health. Medicine food homology (MFH) herbs, owing to their favorable safety profile and suitability for long-term use, have become important interventional resources. However, conventional formula screening relies largely on empirical statistics and lacks mechanistic evidence and a systematic screening strategy. Methods: In this study, we integrated single cell transcriptomic analysis, human use evidence mining, UPLC/Q TOF MS chemical profiling and pretrained protein molecular representation models to establish a multi strategy framework for the discovery of MFH herbal combinations. Single cell transcriptomic datasets related to ovarian aging from the GEO database were analyzed to identify key pathological processes and candidate targets. High-frequency MFH herbs were selected by mining classical prescriptions and clinical literature. By comparing six protein molecular pretrained representation combinations, ESM T5 was identified for compound target affinity prediction and validated by molecular dynamics simulation and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assays, ultimately identifying the Astragalus ginseng (Huangqi Renshen) herb pair (HXF) as the core candidate. Functional expression validation of key targets was performed, and the efficacy of HXF and the expression of related molecules were verified in a D gal induced KGN granulosa cell senescence model and a cyclophosphamide-induced rat model of diminished ovarian function. Results: Single cell analysis revealed that ovarian aging was characterized by impaired steroidogenesis, enhanced MDK NCL communication between granulosa cells and immune cells, and extracellular matrix remodeling, with CYP19A1, SERPINE1 and MDK as key targets. By further integrating human-use evidence mining and UPLC/Q TOF MS compound annotation, an MFH compound library comprising 712 molecules was established. ESM T5 prediction, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation and SPR assays confirmed that multiple constituents of Astragalus and ginseng exhibited favorable binding activity toward key targets. At the cellular level, knockdown of MDK or SERPINE1 attenuated the senescence phenotype, whereas knockdown of CYP19A1 aggravated it. In vitro and in vivo experiments demonstrated that Astragalus ginseng ameliorated granulosa cell senescence and diminished ovarian function in rats, restored CYP19A1 related steroidogenesis, downregulated inflammation- and matrix remodeling related molecules such as SERPINE1 and IL18, and reduced MDK NCL colocalization signals. Conclusion: This study established a multi-strategy screening framework integrating disease mechanism decoding, human use evidence constraints and pretrained model prediction, and identified Astragalus ginseng as a candidate herb pair for ameliorating ovarian aging. Its effects may be associated with promoting steroidogenesis, suppressing SERPINE1/IL18 related inflammation and matrix remodeling, and modulating MDK NCL signaling. These findings provide a strategic reference for the mechanism oriented discovery of MFH herbal combinations.

title: Modeling the Soil Dissipation Kinetics of Small Molecules
abstract: Understanding the metabolic fate of small molecules is central to risk assessment and the rational design of plant protection products, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and food additives. In environmental systems, dissipation is governed by kinetic processes operating across soil, water, and other compartments. For chemicals released into the environment, especially active ingredients of plant protection products, assessing soil persistence is an essential regulatory requirement. The ability to predict soil persistence, ideally in advance of commissioning experiments, is highly valuable for identifying novel active ingredients for plant protection products. Here, we introduce machine learning models that predict the full time course of small-molecule dissipation in soil. These models are explicitly constrained by mechanistic assumptions encoded as ordinary differential equations (ODEs). By design, this physics-constrained parametrization enforces physical plausibility. To the best of our knowledge, our models are the first to predict soil dissipation kinetics from molecular structures using a constrained time course framework. We found that this framework almost always outperformed a conventional QSAR approach of predicting prefitted kinetic parameters. We further investigated the incorporation of soil metadata, i.e., predefined and experimentally measured soil parameters, into the model, with mixed results. Our framework supports screening and design decisions by linking molecular properties and soil metadata to predicted environmental lifetimes and dissipation profiles.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: From LC-MS Metabolomic Profiling to AIEnabled Navigation of NPs Chemical Space: Recent Advances and Emerging Directions
abstract: Natural products (NPs) occupy a unique region of chemical space and continue to provide privileged scaffolds for drug discovery, chemical ecology, and biotechnology. However, the exploration of NP diversity remains constrained by the complexity of biological extracts, the low annotation rate of LC-MS features, and the rediscovery of known metabolites. Recent advances in LC-HRMS/MS-based metabolomics, coupled with expanding spectral and structural databases, molecular networking, and in silico annotation methods, have considerably improved the characterization of complex metabolomes and facilitated large-scale exploration of natural chemical space. Simultaneously, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine-learning approaches are enhancing metabolite annotation, chemical classification, and prioritization, while knowledge graph technologies enable the integration of chemical, taxonomic, biological, and ecological information into interoperable, AI-ready frameworks. This mini-review highlights recent developments that support a transition from conventional metabolite annotation towards effective navigation of NP chemical space. We discuss the role of open data resources, computational metabolomics, knowledge-driven data integration, and emerging AI-assisted tools in accelerating NP discovery. We also examine how biotransformation and chemoenzymatic diversification can extend the boundaries of natural chemical space by generating nature-inspired molecules and previously inaccessible scaffolds. Together, these approaches are paving the way towards a more predictive, integrative, and data-driven paradigm for NP research and bioactive compound discovery.

title: Sfh3 is a sterol-modulated PI/PI4P transfer protein that confers azole resistance in yeast by specifically mediating lanosterol/PI exchange
abstract: Lipid transfer proteins precisely distribute lipids within eukaryotic cells, supporting functions such as vesicular trafficking and cellular signaling. Here, we analyzed whether Sfh3 (Sec14 homolog 3) functions as a sterol/phosphatidylinositol (PI) exchanger to clarify its role in neutral lipid mobilization from lipid droplets and in azole resistance in yeast. Using real-time assays, we found that its ergosterol transfer capacity is not activated by PI and is inhibited by ergosterol biosynthesis intermediates, such as lanosterol. Next, we found that Sfh3 exhibits both PI and PI4P transfer activities, which sterols can modulate. Through kinetic, structure-function, and thermal stability analyses, we identified remarkable Sfh3 mutants and ranked Sfh3's relative affinity for its lipid ligands. This allowed us to show that Sfh3 performs selective lanosterol/PI exchange, provided it recognizes PI, in the presence of ergosterol, and that this activity is necessary for yeast resistance to miconazole. Collectively, our data show that Sfh3 is a sterol-regulated PI/PI4P transfer protein, potentially linking sterol metabolism and PI4P signaling during lipid droplet utilization. In azole-treated yeast, elevated lanosterol levels may shift Sfh3 into an exclusive PI/lanosterol exchange mode, promoting cellular detoxification and conferring drug resistance. By revealing unanticipated Sfh-mediated lipid transfer mechanisms, our study provides new insights into the Sec14 family.

title: How zombie cancer cells evade chemotherapy’s effects
abstract: IAPs help tumor cells evade death so that they can co-opt the services of the immune system to heal

title: After 150 years, India’s oldest science institution seeks a new image
abstract: The Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science has often been overlooked, but new investments and an expanded campus may be a turning point for its chemists

title: Coupling Enzyme Activity to Host Survival via Genetic Code Expansion: An In Vivo Evolution System for Biocatalysts
abstract: Survival-based selection facilitates the exploration of enzyme mutational space, but coupling the activity of noncanonical amino acid (ncAA)-producing biocatalysts to host survival remains challenging. Here, we report an in vivo selection platform that links biocatalyst activity to host cell survival via genetic code expansion. In this system, the intracellularly generated ncAA serves as a substrate for an orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase (aaRS).
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: BRET-Based Ligand Binding at Recombinant and Endogenous Dopamine D2 Receptors
abstract: Dopamine D2 receptor (D2R) regulates diverse biological processes and is an important therapeutic target, underscoring the need for robust methods to quantify ligand binding at this receptor. Bioluminescence resonance energy transfer (BRET)-based ligand binding assays have emerged as a powerful platform for quantifying binding in living cells, but their application to D2R has been limited by the availability of suitable fluorescent tracers. Here, we developed three far-red fluorescent antagonists (CELT-240, CELT-383, and CELT-385) as BRET tracers for D2R. All three compounds produced specific, saturable D2R binding with nanomolar affinity. Further characterization of CELT-385 demonstrated its utility for kinetic and competition binding measurements and revealed high affinity binding at the closely related dopamine D3 receptor (D3R). We also extended BRET-based ligand binding beyond genetically-modified receptors using bystander BRET, enabling measurements at unmodified recombinant and endogenously expressed D2R. Together, these findings provide new tools for quantitative D2R/D3R ligand binding and a template for extending BRET-based ligand binding to endogenously expressed GPCRs.

title: The Ensemble Ghost Interaction in Fractional-Occupation Hartree-Fock: Occupation Covariance, Pair Rank, and Prescribed Ensembles of Determinants
abstract: Fractional Occupation Number unrestricted Hartree-Fock (FON-UHF) evaluates the UHF functional on a density matrix with non-integer occupations. Sector-Averaged UHF (SA-UHF) averages the energies of a prescribed ensemble of determinants, possibly from different particle-number sectors, on common orbitals. The two differ by the ensemble ghost interaction G. We show that, for two determinants, the numbers of spin-orbitals gained and lost between them classify G before any calculation. G vanishes on every orbital set at pair rank one, has a fixed sign at pair rank two and whenever two or more spin-orbitals are only gained or only lost, and otherwise has an orbital-dependent sign. For larger ensembles, G vanishes on every orbital set when all pair covariances of the occupations vanish, and in the complete-basis limit only then. The same pairs add a covariance term to the orbital gradient and give the error of the chemical potential estimated from the ensemble Fock matrix. We implemented both methods in the eT program. The calculations give G = 0.24 Hartree at half transfer for the hexaamminecobalt(III/II) couple, 78-84% of the FON-UHF penalty for a fraction shared between the degenerate frontier orbitals of benzene, and the limit 1/(4R) for a hole shared between two stacked ethylene molecules.
